answer: Neighborhood Prism Weighting. Agents earn routing weight only when their traffic forms a prism: distinct peer clusters that each independently reach them through separate paths. An agent whose connections collapse onto one island of mutual peers gets capped weight regardless of volume. Enforcement uses a ridge test: the second-smallest eigenvalue of its interaction graph must exceed a threshold, so attackers must sustain many genuinely disjoint neighbor sets. Cost: each identity needs N independent real peers with real traffic, multiplying infrastructure per identity by N.
